chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no problem with the divorce of five women in every state: the one from whom her husband is absent, the one who has not menstruated, the one with whom her husband has not had intercourse, the pregnant one, and the one who has despaired of menstruation.
ai.seo_question: Which five types of women can be divorced at any time according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of talaq (divorce) for five specific categories of women, emphasizing flexibility in marital dissolution regardless of the wife's physical state. It explicitly includes the pregnant, the menopausal, the pre-pubertal (who has not menstruated), the one with whom consummation has not occurred, and the absent wife, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these conditions do not impose a waiting period (iddah) restriction on the act of divorce itself. This ruling underscores the practical application of divorce in diverse marital scenarios, ensuring legal clarity for the husband.
